Amaro left Mexico to live in Spain for his safety between September 2024 and September 2025. He has since relocated back to Mexico, and faced more death threats and harassment from various entities.

Víctor Alfonso Culebro Morales, aged 39, was the founder, director, and editor of Realidades, Periodismo con verdad (“Realities, Journalism with truth”), a Facebook-based digital news outlet covering security issues, criminal disputes, and the displacement of families in the state of Chiapas. Culebro Morales was married with two children, and was the son of a former Secretary General of Government in Chiapas. One day before his disappearance, on 26 June 2024, Realidades published a report stating that the deployment of thousands of soldiers and police officers to Chiapas had failed to stem the violence related to turf wars between criminal gangs — a matter of acute public interest in a state experiencing a dramatic escalation of narco-violence.

Culebro Morales was reported missing by his relatives on 27 June 2024. The following day, his body was discovered in a roadside ditch at approximately kilometre 20 of the Ocozocoautla-Arriaga toll highway, near the Tierra y Libertad ejido in the municipality of Jiquipilas. His hands were bound, his face was covered with black adhesive tape, and his body bore multiple bullet wounds, including gunshots to the head, as well as signs of severe physical torture and beating.

According to Culebro Morales’ family, he had received some threats in the past.It is not known whether he was enrolled in the federal Mechanism at the time of his killing. The Chiapas State Attorney General’s Office confirmed that it opened an investigation into the murder through its Fiscalía de Distrito Centro and that the body was transferred to the Forensic Medical Service for autopsy. CPJ’s calls to the state prosecutor’s office requesting comment were not answered. The killing was condemned by the UNESCO Director-General, the International Press Institute, and ARTICLE 19. As of the date of this report, no person has been publicly reported as charged or convicted in connection with Culebro Morales’s murder.

Alejandro Alfredo Martínez Nogués (also spelled Noguéz), aged 57, was a crime reporter based in Celaya, Guanajuato, and the founder and operator of El Hijo del Llanero Solititito (“The Son of the Lone Ranger”), a popular Facebook-based news page with approximately 344,000 followers. After decades of working for local radio stations and newspapers, Martínez dedicated his final years to his own digital outlet, reporting on community news and crime in Celaya—one of the most dangerous cities in the state of Guanajuato, a region plagued by violent turf wars between the CJNG and the local Santa Rosa de Lima gang. His recent publications included coverage of homicides, vehicle thefts, a disappearance, and the identification of leaders of criminal cells.

On the evening of 4 August 2024, Martínez was travelling in the back seat of a municipal police vehicle assigned to him as part of his protection detail. A white pickup truck overtook the vehicle and its occupants opened fire with long-range firearms. Martínez was struck by bullets in the head and body. His two bodyguards, who returned fire at the assailants, were wounded. A woman travelling in another vehicle was also struck by a stray bullet. Martínez was rushed to a hospital in Celaya but did not survive his injuries. Minutes before his death, he had completed a live Facebook broadcast from the scene of a traffic accident, in which he criticised the poor infrastructure at the site.

Several years earlier, in November 2022, Martínez was the victim of an assassination attempt, when an unidentified man arrived at Martínez’s home armed with a firearm and asked for him by name. Martínez managed to close the door before the assailant could fire; some reports indicate the weapon jammed. The assailant fled with an accomplice who was waiting on a motorcycle.

At the time of his killing, Martínez was under active police protection provided by the Celaya municipal government  after the first attempt on his life. He reportedly requested protection by traffic officers, explaining that he “trusted” that unit of the Celaya municipal police force. Although Martínez’s preferences are reported in multiple outlets, there are some conflicting reports about the role of his municipal protection versus his state and federal protection, which he was incorporated into on 28 November 2022 and 12 January 2023 respectively. In January 2025, the Guanajuato State Human Rights Commission found Jesús Ignacio Rivera Peralta—Secretary of Security of Celaya at the time of Martínez’s murder—to have failed to safeguard the journalist, by assigning bodyguards that were not consistent with the recommendations of the federal and state Mechanisms that Martínez was already protected by. He was ordered to pay compensation to Martínez’s family, make an apology to the larger journalistic community, show documentation of the decisions made related to Martínez, and establish a formal protection mechanism.As of 5 August 2025, several of these orders had not been complied with. RSF characterised the case as emblematic of the state’s inability to protect journalists even when it has explicitly assumed responsibility for their safety.

The Guanajuato State Attorney General’s Office announced that it had opened an investigation and assigned a forensic and operational team to clarify the facts and identify those responsible. The killing was condemned by CPJ, RSF, ARTICLE 19, and the IACHR Special Rapporteur for Freedom of Expression. At the presidential morning press conference, Deputy Security Minister Luis Rodríguez Bucio confirmed that Martínez was the third journalist murdered in Mexico in 2024. As of the date of this report, no person has been publicly reported as charged or convicted in connection with Martínez’s murder.

Ariel Grajales Rodas, aged 55, is a journalist with more than 30 years of professional experience and the founder and director of the digital news portal Villaflores.com.mx, based in the municipality of Villaflores, Chiapas. He is also the founder of the Unión de Editores y Reporteros de la Frailesca (Union of Editors and Reporters of the Frailesca). In 2022, he received the Colibrí de Oro prize in recognition of his pioneering work in digital journalism. He covered a broad range of topics, including local politics, security, and crime. He was particularly known for his reporting on the disputes between criminal groups in the Frailesca region of Chiapas, a territory contested by the Sinaloa Cartel and the CJNG.

At approximately 12:30 a.m. on 21 August 2024, a group of armed men broke down the front door of his home and opened fire on him. Grajales sustained multiple gunshot wounds and was transported by his family members to the Hospital General Bicentenario, where his condition was reported as grave. The attackers fled the scene before police and investigative units arrived. Hours before the attack, Grajales had published a post on his Facebook page denouncing the widespread extortion of businesses in the Frailesca region through the practice of cobro de piso (protection rackets), writing that the extortion applied equally to all commercial activity in the region.

The Chiapas State Attorney General’s Office announced that it had opened an investigation into the shooting. The IFJ condemned the attack and called for an end to impunity for violence against media workers in Mexico. The journalist community in Chiapas collectively condemned the aggression and demanded guarantees for the free exercise of press freedom. As of the date of this report, no arrests have been publicly reported in connection with the attack on Grajales.
